# Data Model Specification

This document defines the data entities, attributes, and schemas for the
"Investigating the Effectiveness of Contrastive Loss on Small-World Graphs" project.
It serves as the source of truth for data generation, training artifacts, and analysis results.

## 1. SyntheticGraph

Represents a single Watts-Strogatz small-world graph generated for the study.
Derived from the initial ring lattice, it includes community labels and topological metrics.

**Source**: Generated by `code/data_generation.py` (Task T019).
**Storage**: `data/raw/graphs.jsonl`

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|:--- |:--- |:--- |
| `id` | string | Unique identifier (UUID or hash). |
| `beta` | float | Rewiring probability ($\beta \in [0.0, 1.0]$). |
| `seed` | integer | Random seed used for generation. |
| `node_count` | integer | Number of nodes ($N$). Fixed at 110 per FR-001. |
| `k` | integer | Number of nearest neighbors in the initial ring lattice. |
| `clustering_coefficient` | float | Global clustering coefficient of the graph. |
| `edge_list` | list of list | List of edges `[[src, dst],...]`. |
| `labels` | list of int | Community labels for each node, derived from the initial lattice. |
| `checksum` | string | SHA-256 hash of the graph data for verification. |

### JSON Schema Example (Draft 7)

```json
{
 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
 "title": "SyntheticGraph",
 "type": "object",
 "required": ["id", "beta", "seed", "node_count", "k", "clustering_coefficient", "edge_list", "labels"],
 "properties": {
 "id": { "type": "string", "description": "Unique graph identifier" },
 "beta": { "type": "number", "minimum": 0.0, "maximum": 1.0 },
 "seed": { "type": "integer" },
 "node_count": { "type": "integer", "const": 110 },
 "k": { "type": "integer" },
 "clustering_coefficient": { "type": "number", "minimum": 0.0, "maximum": 1.0 },
 "edge_list": {
 "type": "array",
 "items": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 2, "maxItems": 2 }
 },
 "labels": {
 "type": "array",
 "items": { "type": "integer" },
 "minItems": 110,
 "maxItems": 110
 }
 }
}
```

## 2. TrainingRun

Represents a single training execution of a GCN model on a specific graph using a specific loss function.
Includes the full trajectory of loss and accuracy per epoch.

**Source**: Generated by `code/train.py` (Tasks T026, T027).
**Storage**: `data/processed/trajectories/training_run_{id}_{loss_type}.json`

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|:--- |:--- |:--- |
| `run_id` | string | Unique identifier for the run. |
| `graph_id` | string | Reference to the `SyntheticGraph` used. |
| `loss_type` | string | Either `cross_entropy` or `infonce`. |
| `beta` | float | The $\beta$ parameter of the underlying graph. |
| `epochs_trained` | integer | Total epochs executed (up to `MAX_EPOCHS`). |
| `convergence_status` | string | `converged` or `censored`. |
| `steps_to_convergence` | integer | Epoch index where accuracy $\ge$ `CONVERGENCE_THRESHOLD` (or `MAX_EPOCHS` if censored). |
| `final_accuracy` | float | Accuracy at the last epoch. |
| `trajectory` | list of object | Per-epoch metrics: `[{epoch: int, loss: float, accuracy: float},...]`. |
| `model_weights` | string | Path to the saved model weights (optional, or base64 encoded). |
| `censorship_flag` | boolean | `true` if `convergence_status` is `censored`. |

### JSON Schema Example (Draft 7)

```json
{
 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
 "title": "TrainingRun",
 "type": "object",
 "required": ["run_id", "graph_id", "loss_type", "beta", "epochs_trained", "convergence_status", "steps_to_convergence", "final_accuracy", "trajectory"],
 "properties": {
 "run_id": { "type": "string" },
 "graph_id": { "type": "string" },
 "loss_type": { "type": "string", "enum": ["cross_entropy", "infonce"] },
 "beta": { "type": "number" },
 "epochs_trained": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 },
 "convergence_status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["converged", "censored"] },
 "steps_to_convergence": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 },
 "final_accuracy": { "type": "number", "minimum": 0.0, "maximum": 1.0 },
 "trajectory": {
 "type": "array",
 "items": {
 "type": "object",
 "required": ["epoch", "loss", "accuracy"],
 "properties": {
 "epoch": { "type": "integer" },
 "loss": { "type": "number" },
 "accuracy": { "type": "number" }
 }
 }
 },
 "censorship_flag": { "type": "boolean" }
 }
}
```

## 3. AnalysisResult

Represents the aggregated statistical analysis results from `code/analyze.py`.
Contains the interaction terms and significance flags.

**Source**: Generated by `code/analyze.py` (Tasks T033-T038).
**Storage**: `data/analysis_results.json`

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|:--- |:--- |:--- |
| `tobit_p_value` | float | P-value for the interaction term in Tobit Regression. |
| `tobit_coefficient` | float | Coefficient for the interaction term ($\beta \times$ LossType). |
| `cox_p_value` | float | P-value for the interaction term in Cox PH model. |
| `cox_hazard_ratio` | float | Hazard Ratio for the interaction term. |
| `p_tobit_corr` | float | Bonferroni-corrected p-value for Tobit. |
| `p_cox_corr` | float | Bonferroni-corrected p-value for Cox. |
| `is_significant` | boolean | `true` if `min(p_tobit_corr, p_cox_corr) < 0.05`. |
| `sample_size` | integer | Total number of training runs analyzed. |
| `censored_count` | integer | Number of censored runs in the dataset. |

### JSON Schema Example (Draft 7)

```json
{
 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
 "title": "AnalysisResult",
 "type": "object",
 "required": ["tobit_p_value", "tobit_coefficient", "cox_p_value", "cox_hazard_ratio", "p_tobit_corr", "p_cox_corr", "is_significant", "sample_size"],
 "properties": {
 "tobit_p_value": { "type": "number" },
 "tobit_coefficient": { "type": "number" },
 "cox_p_value": { "type": "number" },
 "cox_hazard_ratio": { "type": "number" },
 "p_tobit_corr": { "type": "number" },
 "p_cox_corr": { "type": "number" },
 "is_significant": { "type": "boolean" },
 "sample_size": { "type": "integer" },
 "censored_count": { "type": "integer" }
 }
}
```

---

## 4. Data Flow Summary

1. **Generation**: `code/data_generation.py` produces `SyntheticGraph` objects -> `data/raw/graphs.jsonl`.
2. **Training**: `code/train.py` consumes graphs, runs dual-loss training -> `TrainingRun` objects -> `data/processed/trajectories/`.
3. **Analysis**: `code/analyze.py` aggregates `TrainingRun` data -> `AnalysisResult` -> `data/analysis_results.json`.
4. **Reporting**: Final report generated from `AnalysisResult` -> `data/report.md`.
